mentions.name: Mains power frequency monitor
mentions.description: Hardware tool that monitors the mains power frequency with resolution of some microseconds, with planned improvements (better code optimization and optocoupler choice) to reach hundreds of nanoseconds of resolution. It can observe grid events such as generators spinning up to maintain frequency, and the original aim was to correlate mains phase jitter with space weather, using the power grid as a sort of radio telescope. The hardware will be open sourced when done.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Ages ago, I had built a tool to monitor the mains power frequency with resolution of some microseconds. I looked at my old assembly code, and realized with better optimization and optocoupler choice, I could probably get that down to some hundreds of nanoseconds.

The original idea was to try and correlate phase jitter to space weather, essentially using the mains power system as a sort of radio telescope. I never did get it working (although I did not have much time to try, either). I was able to see interesting things like generators spinning up to maintain the frequency though.

Will open source the hardware when done.
